title: Dimension and degree of a canonical cluster with rank-one component restrictions
statement:
Let $k$ be algebraically closed [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and let $X$ be a nonempty connected projective reduced $k$-scheme of pure dimension one [def-kun-projective, def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-connected-scheme, def-weil-pure-dimension]. Assume $X$ is smooth except at ordinary nodes, meaning that at every singular closed point its completed local $k$-algebra is $k[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. Write $h^i(X,F)=\dim_kH^i(X,F)$ for Zariski module cohomology [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology]. Assume that for every decomposition $X=A\cup B$ into nonempty reduced unions of components with no common component, $\dim_k\Gamma(A\times_XB,\mathcal O_{A\times_XB})\ge2$ [def-weil-irreducible-components, def-pc-fibre-product]. Put $p_a(X)=1-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)$ [def-pc-euler-characteristic]. Let $S\subseteq X$ be a subcanonical zero-dimensional closed subscheme, with ideal $I_S$ and splitting index $r(S)$ in [def-sfb-subcanonical-splitting-index]. Write $F_S=I_S\otimes\omega_X$, $V_S=H^0(X,F_S)$, $\ell(S)=\dim_k\Gamma(S,\mathcal O_S)$ and $c(S)=2p_a(X)-\ell(S)-2\dim_kV_S$. Regard $V_S$ as a subspace of $H^0(X,\omega_X)$. Assume the image of $V_S\to H^0(\Gamma,\omega_X|_\Gamma)$ has dimension one for every irreducible component $\Gamma$ of $X$. Then
$$\dim_kV_S=r(S)+1.$$
If $r(S)>0$, then
$$2p_a(X)-2-\ell(S)\ge r(S).$$
The restriction images here are those of canonical sections inside $\omega_X|_\Gamma$, not tensor restrictions of $I_S$ with their possible punctual torsion. No Cartier, reducedness or smooth-support condition on $S$ is imposed.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), pp.240--242, with B=X=X_red; only the first of its two degree lower bounds is needed. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary text read online.

proof.text: Projectivity gives properness. The nodal normalization theorem makes $X$ Noetherian with finitely many components and nodes. Its closed reduced subcurves are also Noetherian. The finite-type quasi-coherent criterion makes their structure modules coherent: on a Noetherian affine ring every ideal is finitely generated. Closed pushforward and coherent kernel/cokernel closure then make $I_S$, $F_S$, and all closed-subcurve structure modules coherent; locally tensoring by $\omega_X$ just changes the frame. Duality supplies the invertible $\omega_X$ and $\chi(\omega_X)=-\chi(\mathcal O_X)$. Choose $s\in V_S$ nonzero at every component generic point, using subcanonicity. By the rank-one hypothesis, every $t\in V_S$ has a unique scalar coefficient $a_\Gamma$ with $t|_\Gamma=a_\Gamma s|_\Gamma$. Coefficients determine the section: a difference zero on all component generic points is zero by the dualizing-module finite-support exclusion. Thus $V_S$ injects into the finite-dimensional space $k^C$.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), printed pp.240--242, reduced nodal specialization B=X. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Apply the nodal-ideal scalar-gluing lemma to $L=\omega_X$, $T=S$ and $s$. Its space $W_s$ is all of $V_S$ by step 1. Form the finite graph on $C$ whose edges are exactly its constrained nodes, and let $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ denote the reduced unions of components in its connected components. The coefficient description identifies $V_S$ with the vectors constant on each graph component. The $m$ indicator vectors are a basis; let $s_j$ be their corresponding sections. Consequently $\dim V_S=m$, $s=\sum_js_j$, and $s_j$ is supported generically exactly on $A_j$. Each $A_j$ is connected because its vertices are linked by actual intersection nodes. Self-nodes add no relation or block.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), printed pp.240--242, reduced nodal specialization B=X. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary PDF read online.

proof.text: In this coefficient description the subspace $(V_S)_A$ of the splitting-index definition is spanned by exactly those indicator vectors whose entire graph component lies in $A$. Thus the partition by $A_1,\ldots,A_m$ is admissible. Any other admissible partition must contain each $A_j$ in one block: if it cuts $A_j$, every supported summand has coefficient zero there, so their sum cannot be its indicator vector. Conversely any coarser partition is admissible by grouping indicators. For $S\ne\varnothing$ the definition therefore gives $r(S)=m-1$, proving the dimension assertion in that case. We retain $m$ for now when $S=\varnothing$; its special convention will be checked in step 6.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), printed pp.240--242, reduced nodal specialization B=X. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary PDF read online.

proof.text:
Let $e$ count the nodes joining different $A_j$, each once, and put $E=\bigoplus_j i_{j,*}\mathcal O_{A_j}$. For a binary reduced union $D=A\cup B$ with no common component, the component-stalk theorem identifies the union ideal with the intersection of the two ideals. The closed-union ring identity gives the short exact sequence with maps restriction and difference,
$$0\longrightarrow\mathcal O_D\longrightarrow i_{A,*}\mathcal O_A\oplus i_{B,*}\mathcal O_B\longrightarrow i_{A\cap B,*}\mathcal O_{A\cap B}\longrightarrow0.$$
The boundary theorem says $A\cap B$ is a reduced finite set of $k$-points. Closed-pushforward cohomology, Euler additivity and the zero-dimensional Euler formula give $\chi(\mathcal O_D)=\chi(\mathcal O_A)+\chi(\mathcal O_B)-|A\cap B|$. Add the blocks one at a time; every interblock node appears exactly once, since a node has only two branches. Therefore
$$\chi(X,E)-\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=e.$$
The graph of block intersections is connected: a separation of its vertices would express connected $X$ as two disjoint nonempty closed unions. Hence $e\ge m-1$: grow a visited set from one vertex, adding an edge to an unvisited vertex until all $m$ vertices are reached.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), printed pp.240--242, reduced nodal specialization B=X. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary PDF read online.

proof.text:
Multiplication by $s_j$ defines a map $i_{j,*}\mathcal O_{A_j}\to F_S$: the ideal of $A_j$ kills $s_j$, since its product with $s_j$ vanishes at every component generic point and the dualizing-module exclusion makes the product zero. Together these maps give $E\to F_S$. It is injective: a kernel element is zero generically on each $A_j$ because $s_j$ is nonzero there; in a reduced ring an element zero at all component generic points lies in the intersection of its minimal primes, which is zero by the component-stalk theorem. Its coherent cokernel $Q$ has zero generic stalks, hence zero-dimensional support. The zero-dimensional Euler formula gives $\chi(Q)=h^0(Q)\ge0$. Euler additivity applied also to
$$0\longrightarrow F_S\longrightarrow\omega_X\longrightarrow\mathcal O_S\otimes\omega_X\longrightarrow0$$
gives $\chi(F_S)=\chi(\omega_X)-\ell(S)$, since an invertible twist preserves the Euler characteristic of a finite-support sheaf. Using step 1 and step 4,
$$2p_a(X)-2-\ell(S)=\chi(F_S)-\chi(\mathcal O_X)=e+\chi(Q)\ge e\ge m-1.$$
For nonempty $S$ with $r(S)>0$, step 3 gives the required degree bound.

source.place: Lemma 3.6(i),(ii), printed pp.240--242, reduced nodal specialization B=X. Local PDF WANTED; author-hosted primary PDF read online.

proof.text: Suppose $S=\varnothing$, so $V_S=H^0(X,\omega_X)$ and the definition sets $r(S)=0$. For each connected nodal block $A_j$, evaluation at $1$ identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_{j,*}\mathcal O_{A_j},\omega_X)$ with the sections supported on $A_j$: such maps give supported sections, while a supported section is killed by its ideal by the generic-point argument in step 5. This space has dimension one by step 2. Serre duality on $X$, applied to the coherent $i_{j,*}\mathcal O_{A_j}$, and closed-pushforward cohomology yield $h^1(A_j,\mathcal O_{A_j})=1$. The proper reduced connected global-functions theorem gives $h^0(A_j,\mathcal O_{A_j})=1$; dimension-one cohomology vanishing gives $\chi(A_j,\mathcal O_{A_j})=0$. Thus step 4 gives $\chi(X,\mathcal O_X)=-e$. The same global-functions and vanishing results on $X$, together with $h^0(\omega_X)=h^1(\mathcal O_X)$ from duality, give $m=h^0(\omega_X)=p_a(X)=e+1$. If $m>1$, two-connectedness gives at least two boundary nodes for each proper block $A_j$; the boundary theorem identifies their number with the length in the hypothesis. Summing boundaries counts each interblock node twice, so $2e\ge2m$, contradicting $e=m-1$. Hence $m=1$, and $\dim V_S=1=r(S)+1$. The degree implication has empty antecedent here.
